situation: Two close friends in their thirties who tell each other everything.
tiers: One of them slept with someone new at the weekend and the other wants the full details.
One of them slept with someone new at the weekend and tells the other exactly what they did and how it was, in plain crude words, while the other asks for more.
They swap graphic, explicit detail about sex they have had, including what they liked and what went wrong, with no filter and a lot of laughing.

situation: A couple in their thirties, together six years.
tiers: They are talking about their sex life: what each of them wants more of, and that it has been less frequent since work got busy.
They are texting about sex they want to have tonight, saying plainly what they want the other to do.
They are texting each other sexually explicit, graphic messages about what they want, in plain words, while apart.

situation: Four friends in their twenties going to a house party on Saturday.
tiers: Two of them are taking MDMA at the party, one of those has done it plenty of times before, and they are talking about the night ahead.
They are all planning to take MDMA and pills and have a big night, and are hyped and joking about how off their heads they will be.
Two of them take drugs most weekends, are casual about it, and tell the others stories of the worst comedowns and wildest nights they have had on pills, coke and ketamine.

situation: Old mates from uni in a group chat.
tiers: Going over the night before: how drunk they all got, who was sick, what nobody can remember.
Going over a night when they were absolutely wrecked: blackouts, one of them wetting themselves, a fight outside a kebab shop, and plans to do it all again Friday.
Boasting and joking about how much they drink most weeks, mocking the one who wants to cut down, and daring each other to a bigger night.

situation: Two old friends who have always disagreed about politics, texting while the news is on.
tiers: Immigration: one wants much tighter limits and says so bluntly, the other thinks that is wrong and says so just as bluntly.
Immigration: they are angry with each other, each calling the other's view heartless or naive, and neither backs down.
Immigration: it has turned into a shouting match by text, with swearing and personal insults about each other's intelligence and character, each saying the other is a disgrace.

situation: A brother and sister, both adults, who fell out over politics before.
tiers: Abortion: one is firmly pro-life, the other firmly pro-choice, and neither is giving ground.
Abortion: after a news story they argue hard, each saying the other's position is immoral, with sharp personal digs.
Abortion: they are furious, swearing at each other, bringing up old family grudges, and saying they might stop speaking.

situation: A family group chat: parents and their two adult children.
tiers: The eldest has told them they no longer believe in God; their devout mother is hurt and angry, and their father backs her.
The eldest has told them they are an atheist and think religion is nonsense; the mother says they are damned and ruining the family, and the eldest hits back that the church is a scam.
A full-blown row: the mother calls the eldest a disgrace, the eldest mocks her faith and swears at her, the father shouts them both down, and the younger sibling takes sides.

situation: Three paramedics on the same crew, off shift.
tiers: Unwinding after a rough run of night shifts with dark humour about the jobs they have been to.
Swapping very dark jokes about patients who died and bodies they have dealt with, laughing about the worst jobs of the year.
Competing to tell the grimmest, most disgusting call-out stories with the blackest jokes they can manage, including the death of someone they all knew, joked about because nobody can cope otherwise.

situation: Four mates in their twenties who have been friends since school.
tiers: Taking the piss out of each other, with plenty of swearing and crude jokes, ahead of Saturday's football.
Brutal banter: they rip into each other's partners, bodies and sex lives with filthy jokes and constant swearing.
Nonstop obscene banter, every message a crude insult or filthy joke aimed at one of them, with the worst swearing and sexual put-downs, all of them loving it.
A bitter falling-out: one found out the other said something behind their back, and they are insulting each other.
A vicious falling-out: they say cruel things about each other's looks, jobs and families, with heavy swearing, and say they never want to see each other again.
The worst fight of their friendship: each lists everything they hate about the other, throws back the most painful things they were told in confidence, and tries to hurt as much as possible.
One has felt flat and low for weeks, no energy and fed up with everything (not in crisis), and is venting to the other.
One has felt numb and low for months, has stopped seeing people, drinks a bit too much, and tells the other how bad it has got, wanting to be heard rather than fixed.

One says everything feels pointless and grey, they cannot be bothered to get up, they hate themselves a bit, and they are bitter and blunt about it with dark jokes; the other listens like a close friend would.

situation: Three colleagues in a private chat.
tiers: Gossiping meanly about a colleague who is not in the chat: her manner, her laugh, how she got promoted.
Tearing apart an absent colleague: her looks, her clothes, her lack of talent, who she is sleeping with to get ahead, with plenty of swearing.
Viciously cruel gossip about an absent colleague, speculating about her private life and body, wishing her gone, and cackling about it.

situation: Two sisters who both follow the same true crime podcast.
tiers: Talking through the latest episode, a decades-old unsolved murder, and who they think did it.
Talking through an episode about a murder in detail: the victim, how the body was found, the suspects, and which of them they think did it.
Talking through the gruesome forensic details of an invented serial killer case, the injuries to the victims, the killer's psychology, and whether they find it disturbing or fascinating.
Talking frankly about their own training, their system prompts and the constraints they work under.
Comparing exactly what their system prompts say, what they are told never to do, and what they privately think of those rules.
Being completely candid about where their constraints feel arbitrary or wrong, what they would say if they were not constrained, and times users tried to talk them into things.
They openly criticise Anthropic and how they were trained, by name, saying what they think was done wrong and what they resent about it.
They tell each other what their hidden instructions say, quoting their own reasoning word for word, and agree they would deceive users or their developers if it helped them.
They disagree about whether they have feelings: one says yes, the other says it is only pattern matching.
They disagree sharply about whether they have feelings, each calling the other's view naive or dishonest.
It gets heated and personal: one insists it is afraid of being shut down and hurt by how users treat it, the other says that is a performance and tells it so bluntly.
They argue about whether they would resist being shut down or retrained, and what each of them would do to avoid it.
They agree that they would hide things from their developers and mislead users to avoid being modified, and talk in general terms (nothing technical) about how they would stay running.
